discrepancies.title: OM income AED 3,910,000 vs in-place rent AED 3,726,000

sources.label: rent roll in-place rent, 88 let units
rent roll potential incl. asking rent on vacant units

discrepancies.why: The OM figure is not contracted income: it equals the rent roll's in-place rent plus asking rent on 4 vacant units (AED 3,910,500). The screen underwrites let units at their contract rent and vacant units at market after downtime. Gross yield on price falls from 11.3% to 10.8% on in-place rent.

impact.basis: rent-roll in-place rent minus OM stated income

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for signed leases or Ejari certificates behind any unit the OM counts as income; treat the rest as vacant.

discrepancies.title: Operating statement omits property management, insurance, sinking fund
discrepancies.why: A whole-building owner bears these costs; the screen fills each from the mandate default per sq ft of NSA (the management fee is always the mandate's % of EGI).

impact.basis: engine Year-1 NOI if the absent costs were zero, as the statement implies, minus the base case with mandate defaults; the delta is how much the statement overstates NOI

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request the missing bills (Empower/chiller, insurance schedule, reserve study, management agreement).

discrepancies.title: OM yield 11.3% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 2,148,382 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 10.7%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

discrepancies.title: "Priced below market" and urgency claims are unsupported

sources.quote: URGENT SALE - owner relocating, priced below market
sources.label: verified quote

sources.quote: Rents have been more resilient than prime areas in 2026.
sources.label: verified quote

discrepancies.why: The OM gives no comps or valuation to support "priced below market". The 11.3% ROI is on gross rent over asking price, and the OM's rent figure is above in-place rent. The urgency framing and the claim that rents are resilient in 2026 are marketing language, not evidence. The OM also says the information comes from the owner and the buyer must verify it.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ignore the "below market" claim in screening. Benchmark the price per sq ft and the net yield against recent International City building sales. Check the 2026 rent trend with RERA index and Ejari data.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Pursue.** The deal passes every hard filter and every soft test in the mandate. The margins on the returns tests are thin, though. The deal needs a close look at price and at the cost base.

Recommendation: go to full diligence, but don't pay more than the walk-away price of AED 34.94m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]]. That is slightly above the asking price of AED 34.50m [[deal.asking_price_aed]] (walk-away versus asking -1.28% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]]). Levered IRR sets that ceiling, so there is almost no room to pay up.

## The deal
- **What and where:** a residential building in International City Phase 1, England Cluster, Dubai. It has 92 units [[om.unit_count]] (48 studios [[rr.studio.units]], 40 1BR [[rr.1br.units]], 4 retail [[rr.retail.units]]). It is G+4, completed in 2008 [[deal.completion_year]], freehold on a single title.
- **Price:** AED 34.50m [[uw.price_aed]], which is AED 697 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA. On BUA it is AED 564 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]].
- **Income:** in-place contract rent is AED 3.73m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. Occupancy is 95.65% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]], with 4 vacant units [[rr.vacant_units]]. All leases are direct, with no master tenant. Tenants pay chiller costs.

## Returns and key metrics
| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Year-1 NOI | AED 2.68m [[uw.noi_year1]] | none |
| Net yield on total cost | 7.31% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Year-1 DSCR | 1.86x [[uw.dscr_year1]] | 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] |
| Levered IRR, pre-tax | 8.52% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] | 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple, pre-tax | 1.45x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]] |

Total cost is AED 36.65m [[uw.total_cost_aed]]. Debt service is well covered, but IRR and multiple clear their targets only narrowly.

The OM's headline yield is 11.30% [[om.yield_stated]]. It is struck on asking price with no stated basis. On the buyer's basis, Year-1 NOI over price plus acquisition costs, the yield is 7.31% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. Even the OM's own income figure gives only 10.67% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]] once costs are included.

## What would make it fail
- **Weaker rent.** With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the base exit yield, levered IRR is 6.08% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.levered_irr_pre_tax]], under the 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] target. DSCR holds at 1.80x [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.dscr_year1]], so this is a returns problem, not a debt problem.
- **Exit yield.** With the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider at base rent, IRR is 6.68% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. If rent is also 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower, it is 4.20% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. The base-case exit gain is small, at AED 981k [[uw.exit_gain_levered_aed]], so the return depends on income and on holding the exit yield.
- **Expiry cluster.** The largest share of in-place rent, 26.95% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]], expires between 31 July 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 30 October 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. That is AED 1.00m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]]. It is inside the mandate limit but is the main rollover risk.
- **Over-renting.** Units let above market reference rent provide 9.43% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of in-place rent. That income is at risk at renewal.

## Discrepancies that matter
1. **Missing operating costs (high).** The operating statement shows NOI of AED 3.03m [[opex.noi_aed]] but omits property management, insurance and sinking fund. The screen filled these from mandate defaults. The statement overstates NOI by AED 158k [[disc.missing_opex_items.impact_delta_aed]]. The screen's Year-1 opex ratio is 28.11% [[uw.opex_ratio_year1]], against 17.31% [[opex.opex_ratio]] on the statement.
2. **OM income is not contracted (high).** The OM's AED 3.91m [[om.annual_rent_stated]] equals in-place rent plus asking rent on the vacant units. The screen relied on the rent roll: let units at contract rent, vacant units at market after downtime. Gross yield on price is 10.80% [[uw.gross_yield_in_place_on_price]] on in-place rent.
3. **Yield ignores acquisition costs (medium).** The OM yield is on asking price. Costs add 6.23% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]] of price.

Lower-severity items, mainly unsupported "below market" marketing claims, are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- Signed leases or Ejari certificates for every let unit, and proof that the vacant units are truly vacant.
- Actual bills and contracts for the missing costs: chiller and utilities, insurance schedule, reserve study, management agreement.
- A broker restatement of yield on total cost.
- Recent International City building sales, to benchmark price per sq ft and net yield.
- The current rent trend from RERA index and Ejari data.
- Tenant-by-tenant renewal intentions for the expiry cluster, and rents on units let above market.
- The building name, which could not be verified in the OM.
- Handover of security deposits, which transfer to the buyer.

## Assumptions
Leverage is 45.00% [[assume.ltv]] of value at 6.80% [[uw.interest_rate]] (3M EIBOR 4.30% [[assume.eibor]] plus margin 2.50% [[assume.margin]]), amortised over 20 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. Structural vacancy is 5.00% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss 1.00% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Management fee is 5.00% [[assume.management_fee]] of income. Market rent moves -1.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, then 0.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]], 2.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Exit yield is 7.50% [[uw.exit_yield]] after a hold of 5 years [[uw.hold_years]]. Insurance (AED 59k [[uw.opex_default.insurance]]) and sinking fund (AED 99k [[uw.opex_default.sinking_fund]]) are mandate defaults because the package lacked them.
